Brief: Tell me about the Rosetta mission and what it found at comet 67P. — about Locating Philae

Kept:
1. By April 2015, the image of the lander was successfully identified among several candidates through an in-depth analysis of OSIRIS-NAC data by Guillaume Faury.
2. The breakthrough was achieved when a pre-landing image from the OSIRIS-NAC collection was found to have geometric conditions (illumination and viewing angles) very similar to a post-landing image taken in mid-December 2014.
3. The candidate was definitively confirmed as the Philae lander in September 2016, when the Rosetta spacecraft flew close enough to capture very high-resolution images of the probe resting in a dark crevice.

Named:
